Chapter Details: Status of national population, civil, address, land, business, electoral, tax and social protection registers. 44 variables in 8 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Does the government maintain a digital civil register?
Comments: eCRVS system launched 2022 by Ministry of Health for births, biometric, online registration at crvs.gm; mass campaign registered 1.17M.
revision_notes: All three original sources fetched and support the score. Biometric Update (Aug 2022) and the WCC Group deployment announcement confirm the Ministry of Health launched the HERA eCRVS system in August 2022, replacing paper-based birth registration. The World Bank results brief (Mar 2024) confirms the eCRVS became the foundational system for cross-agency interoperability via a unique national ID number, with 1.17m people (over half the population) registered between Aug 2022 and Feb 2023. Foroyaa (Jun 2024) quotes the Deputy Director of Civil Registration stating digital birth certificate issuance is ongoing in all public health facilities nationwide. Coverage of digital death and marriage registration is not evidenced in any source found, so full national deployment across all vital-event types cannot be confirmed. Score of 4 (Partially deployed) is confirmed rather than raised to the scale maximum of 5, given this gap in evidence for deaths/marriages and campaign uptake still around half the population.
revised_comments: The Gambia operates an electronic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (eCRVS) system, launched in August 2022 by the Ministry of Health using WCC's HERA platform, which replaced the previous paper-based birth registration process. The system issues digital birth certificates linked to a unique national identification number and is used in public health facilities across the country. A national mass registration campaign between August 2022 and February 2023 registered close to 1.17 million people, over half the population, for birth certificates and national health insurance simultaneously, and registration continues on an ongoing basis nationwide. Digital coverage of death and marriage registration is less well documented.
